title: Raspberry and Rose Water Granita
changes_from_base: Raspberries with a small syrup and rose water replace the strawberries; the purée is sieved and chilled before freezing.
summary: Refreshing raspberries and delicate rose water are frozen and scraped into a light, icy dessert perfect for warm afternoons.

steps.title: Syrup
steps.text: Combine 60 ml water and 65 g caster sugar in a small saucepan. Bring to the boil and simmer until dissolved, then leave to cool.

steps.title: Blend
steps.text: Place 680 g raspberries in a blender with the cooled syrup and ½ tsp rose water. Process until the mixture is smooth.

steps.title: Strain
steps.text: Pass the raspberry puree through a fine sieve into a bowl to remove the seeds. Chill the mixture for 2 h or overnight.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Chill a 23 x 28 cm dish in the freezer. Use a stick blender to process the chilled raspberry liquid for 30 seconds before pouring it into the cold dish.

steps.title: First freeze
steps.text: Place the dish in the freezer. Every 30 min, use a fork to scrape the ice crystals from the edges to the centre.

steps.title: Scrape
steps.text: Continue scraping every 30 min until the mixture is evenly frozen but not solid. If it sets too hard, cut into chunks and pulse in a food processor.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Spoon the light raspberry crystals into chilled glasses. Soften the granita in the fridge for 15 min before serving if it has become too firm.

tips: Use the freshest raspberries possible for the most vibrant colour and flavour.
Ensure the dish is thoroughly chilled before adding the liquid to speed up the freezing process.
Adjust the rose water carefully as the floral notes can become very strong.
storage: Keep the granita covered in the freezer for up to 1 week and use a fork to fluff the crystals before serving.
